question.problem:
Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_{120}$ be a random sample of size $n = 120$ from a population with a population mean $\mu = 100$ and population standard deviation $\sigma = 60.$ Find an approximation for the probability that the sample mean is between $102$ and $105.$ *Hint: Two tables of values of $\Phi(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $\Phi(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\, 0.07 \,$$\, 0.08 \,$$\, 0.09 \,$
$\, 0.2 \,$ $\, 0.6064 \,$ $\, 0.6103 \,$ $\, 0.6141 \,$
$\, 0.3 \,$ $\, 0.6443 \,$ $\, 0.6480 \,$ $\, 0.6517 \,$
$\, 0.4 \,$ $\, 0.6808 \,$ $\, 0.6844 \,$ $\, 0.6879 \,$

$z$$\, 0.00 \,$$\, 0.01 \,$$\, 0.02 \,$
$\, 0.7 \,$ $\, 0.7580 \,$ $\, 0.7611 \,$ $\, 0.7642 \,$
$\, 0.8 \,$ $\, 0.7881 \,$ $\, 0.7910 \,$ $\, 0.7939 \,$
$\, 0.9 \,$ $\, 0.8159 \,$ $\, 0.8186 \,$ $\, 0.8212 \,$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with a population mean $\mu$ and population standard deviation $\sigma.$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overline{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overline{X}\sim N\!\left(\mu,\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\right).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
n = 120, \qquad
\mu = 100, \qquad
\sigma = 60.
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(100,\frac{{60}^{2}}{120}) \\  & ∼N(100,30).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(102 \lt \overline{X} \lt  105).$ So, we convert $\overline{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(102<\overset{―}{X}<105) & =P(\frac{102-100}{\sqrt{30}}<Z<\frac{105-100}{\sqrt{30}}) \\  & =P(\frac{2}{\sqrt{30}}<Z<\frac{5}{\sqrt{30}}) \\  & ≈P(0.37<Z<0.91) \\  & =P(Z<0.91)-P(Z<0.37) \\  & =Φ(0.91)-Φ(0.37)\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.37)=0.6443, \\ Φ(0.91)=0.8186.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(102<\overset{―}{X}<105) & =Φ(0.91)-Φ(0.37) \\  & =0.8186-0.6443 \\  & =0.1743.\end{aligned}
$$
